body: I just made a bizzare discovery: this crash only happens when I have my external display connected. Here are my display details: I will update the issue information accordingly.

> Here is [a repository that causes the issue for me](https://github.com/austinlongmn/programming-competition-2025-04-03).

Do you reproduce the issue if you clone this repo to a new location, or only with the existing copy you have locally?

The crash may be related to files in the `res://.godot` folder which isn't part of the Git repository (as expected). Notably metadata for which screen index was last used, which may cause running some code with incorrect bounds that crashes.

Note: I'm on Linux and haven't tested if I could reproduce it.
Even with a fresh clone (no .godot directory), opening the project still causes the crash. I also tried deleting `~/Library/Application Support/Godot`.

I just tried installing Godot on a computer that had never had it installed and I could not reproduce the issue (although, that was an Intel Mac, not an Apple Silicon). I tried deleting `~/Library/Application Support/Godot`, `~/Library/Caches/Godot`, and `.godot` to no avail on my Silicon Mac. The crash still happens every time.
Here are the [macOS panic logs](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20068593/problem-2.log), although I don't know if they will be much help.

` ...../Godot/Godot.4.4.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --rendering-driver vulkan `. [docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html)

Please try this in a terminal window; does it also crash? (Force Vulkan API)

```
Godot Engine v4.4.stable.official.4c311cbee - https://godotengine.org
Vulkan 1.2.283 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: Apple - Apple M1
```

I tried it with Vulkan, but that had no effect.

I did make another interesting discovery, however. The issue only happens when I have HiDPI set at 3008x1692 (see the image above). I changed it to 1440p and the issue didn't come up. I haven't tried it at any of the other settings yet, though.

I configured my external display to the same resolution on my Apple Silicon MacBook Pro, and it did not crash.

We need a full crash log to be able to troubleshoot it more – unfortunately the one you provided only has minimal information.
OK, interesting. Is your display natively 3840x2160? I'm wondering if it is related to the scale. Regardless, how would I obtain the logs you are referring to?
I will update to macOS 15.5 soon and see if that resolves the issue, too.

Can't reproduce it, M4 Pro Mac mini, my main display is set to exactly same resolution:
